Proposed solution: AI checks each document at upload; clean applications move forward; uncertain cases go to reviewers.
Proposed success metric: First AI feedback ≤5 minutes; first human review target <2 hours.
How to measure: Upload timestamp to first AI result; separately, submission to REVIEW_STARTED.
Important caveat: Targets are proposed, not historical results.

Evidence from dataset: 774/3000 = 25.8% of started applications had DOC_RETURNED events.
Proposed solution: Image quality checks, OCR, cross-document name/DOB comparison before formal review.
How to measure: Unique applications with DOC_RETURNED / applications started.
Important caveat: 13.5% projection assumes image-only cases can be prevented; validate in pilot.

Evidence from dataset: 71 applicants had multiple correction events; 75 extra events beyond one per returned applicant.
Proposed solution: Collect all available findings and send one consolidated WhatsApp correction message.
Proposed success metric: One consolidated correction message per correction cycle.
How to measure: Count correction messages sent per application and correction cycles.
Important caveat: Verify message logs; correction events are not necessarily WhatsApp messages.

Proposed solution: Plain-language issue list, direct upload links, reminders and status visibility.
How to measure: No-response within 10 days / unique correction recipients.
Important caveat: If denominator remains 774, nonresponders must fall to 77 or fewer.

Evidence from dataset: Median 8.42 days from application to certification.
Proposed solution: Remove avoidable wait and correction loops; monitor each stage separately.
How to measure: Define start/end timestamps; report final certification separately from KYC-ready stage.
Important caveat: Rulebook requires 15 hours of training before exam; final certification <5 hours conflicts with current process.

Evidence from dataset: 482 of 2,217 verified applicants (21.7%) never started training; accounts for 50.7% of all dropouts.
Proposed solution: Instant KYC feedback (<5 mins) + automated WhatsApp nudge with direct single-sign-on link to training LMS while intent is fresh.
How to measure: Elapsed time from KYC verification to training start; count of verified applicants who drop before training.
Important caveat: Requires seamless API integration between onboarding engine and learning management system (LMS).

Problem / opportunity: High ops cost and manual touches
Evidence from dataset: 9,920 manual touches (3.31/app); ~₹14.9 Lakhs spent Jan–Sep across 22 reviewers.
Proposed solution: Straight-through processing for clean files (≥60%); AI copilot summaries for remaining cases to cut review time to <5 mins.
Proposed success metric: Average manual touches ≤1.2 per application; reviewer minutes <5 mins/app; ops cost reduced by >70%.
How to measure: Track manual touches per app in applications log; measure active reviewer seconds on routed dashboard.
Important caveat: Human reviewers must remain in the loop for edge cases (name mismatch rejection, face match 0.60–0.75).

Problem / opportunity: Late rejection for existing POSP registration
Evidence from dataset: 75 applicants (23.9% of all rejections) rejected for ALREADY_REGISTERED after submitting all 6 docs and waiting in queue.
Proposed solution: Front-load IRDAI registry lookup as 'Step 0' when applicant enters PAN, before requesting document uploads.
Proposed success metric: 0 reviewer touches wasted on pre-registered applicants; immediate eligibility feedback to applicant.
How to measure: Time from PAN entry to IRDAI registry response; count of pre-upload disqualifications.
Important caveat: Assumes IRDAI POSP registry API has real-time availability and acceptable latency.

Problem / opportunity: Reviewer inconsistency on Indian name variants
Evidence from dataset: ~2.5% document verdict error rate; 199 hard cases in 600-app test set with initials, swapped order, or middle names.
Proposed solution: Deterministic name matching algorithm implementing Section 5 of rulebook (treating initials, swaps, and middle names as matches).
Proposed success metric: Decision accuracy ≥95% against application_truth; REJECT recall ≥98%.
How to measure: Confusion matrix on 600-application test set; audit trail of cited matching rule per application.
Important caveat: Hard rejections for NAME_MISMATCH must always be routed to a human for final confirmation per DPDP/compliance rules.
